topics: 7. Vitamins Classification: Fat-Soluble (A, D, E, K) vs Water-Soluble (C & B-Complex; Exception: B₁₂ is Stored in Liver)
7.1 Master Vitamin Pathology Matrix: Vit A (Xerophthalmia, Nyctalopia), Vit B₁ (Beri-Beri), Vit B₂ (Cheilosis), Vit B₃ (Pellagra)
Vit B₁₂ (Pernicious Anemia), Vit C (Scurvy / Collagen Hydroxylation), Vit D (Rickets / Osteomalacia), Vit K (Clotting Factors II, VII, IX, X)
8. Hormones Chemical Taxonomy: Steroids (Cortisol, Sex Hormones), Peptides (Insulin, Glucagon), Amino Acid Derivatives (Epinephrine, Melatonin)
quickSummary: Vitamins are fat-soluble (A, D, E, K; stored in liver/adipose) or water-soluble (C and B-complex; excreted in urine; exception: B₁₂ stored in liver). Key pathologies: Vit A (Xerophthalmia, night blindness), Vit B₁ (Beri-Beri), Vit B₂ (Cheilosis), Vit B₃ (Pellagra 3 D's), Vit B₁₂ (Pernicious anemia), Vit C (Scurvy), Vit D (Rickets/Osteomalacia), Vit K (delayed clotting). Hormones are steroids, peptides, or amino acid derivatives.
summary: Master vitamin classifications, deficiency pathologies, and hormone chemical categories.

summaryBox.takeaway: Vit A: Xerophthalmia/Night blindness. B₁: Beri-Beri. B₂: Cheilosis. B₃: Pellagra (3 D's). B₁₂: Pernicious anemia. C: Scurvy. D: Rickets. K: Delayed clotting.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
VITAMIN CLASSIFICATIONS
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
  FAT-SOLUBLE VITAMINS                                      WATER-SOLUBLE VITAMINS
  Vitamins A, D, E, K                                       Vitamin C & B-Complex
  ├── Soluble in lipids; stored in liver/adipose            ├── Excreted in urine; cannot be stored
  └── Excess causes **Hypervitaminosis**                    └── **Exception:** Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ is stored in liver!

quickRevision: Fat-soluble: A, D, E, K (stored in liver and adipose).
Water-soluble: B-complex, C (excreted in urine; B₁₂ is stored in liver).
Vitamin A: Retinol ──► Xerophthalmia, Night blindness (Nyctalopia).
Vitamin B₂: Riboflavin ──► Cheilosis (mouth corner cracking).
Vitamin B₃: Niacin ──► Pellagra (Dermatitis, Diarrhea, Dementia).
Vitamin C: Ascorbic Acid ──► Scurvy (impaired collagen hydroxylation).
Vitamin K: Phylloquinone ──► Delayed blood clotting (Factors II, VII, IX, X).
keyFormulae: \text{Fat-Soluble: Vitamins A, D, E, K}; \quad \text{Water-Soluble: Vitamins B-Complex, C (B}_{12} \text{ stored in liver)}
